top_choice_rationale: P001 (Pakes, Berry, Levinsohn) recognises a mature, jointly authored measurement advance: estimating demand and competition in differentiated-product markets with endogenous prices. It made substitution patterns, markups and merger and welfare counterfactuals recoverable from market data that reduced-form work could not support. It has about three decades of use in academic work and regulatory practice, has spread into trade, health and environmental economics, and its sensitivities to instruments, functional form and numerics are documented. The credit boundary is clean, since the 1995 paper has three authors, so the citation does not need an arbitrary cut. It rests on a method-level unit that leaves the dynamic-industry and production-function work as context. The main reservations are toolkit versus discovery and the omission of Bresnahan, which I treat as a judgement about framing and not as a merit gap. These do not outweigh the case for an award, so no award ranks below it.
